div.p: Real-time embedded systems require sufficient resources to meet the application's requirements. This often creates over-provisioning of resources, increasing the unused resources and overall costs. Determining optimal resource supply is essential to avoid over-resource provisioning. Existing research works lack consideration of finding the optimized supply of resources to meet the workload demand during any time intervals. Therefore, we propose a resource-aware optimization model to minimize the resource provision in any periodic task model. The proposed approach exploits the supply and demand bound functions to reduce resource over-provisioning while guaranteeing task deadlines. The preliminary experimental results show the benefits of our proposed approach for enhancing resource usage.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Nowadays, real-time embedded systems are evolving with increased functionalities; it requires efficient design and analysis of resources (i.e., computation) to meet their timing requirements. A resource model depicts the aspects of a resource supply and demand for analyzing task schedulability and facilitating the design of resource provisioning. The studies [4] for finding optimal resource allocation in embedded systems demonstrate how to optimally assign the limited resources to meet the demands minimizing total costs. Inaccurate estimation of resource allocation may lead to resource overprovisioning or under-provisioning. Although existing realtime scheduling algorithms examine the task schedulability using supply and demand bound functions, there is a lack of analysis on optimizing the supply of resources to minimize over-provisioning.

Therefore, finding a resource-aware optimization technique is essential to avoid excessive resource usage while meeting the tasks' requirements (e.g., deadline). This paper presents an approach for estimating optimal resource provision by minimizing the difference between supply and demand bound functions of a periodic resource model. The experimental results illustrate the applicability of our proposed approach by comparing our estimated resource with the resource calculated using the traditional linear supply and demand bound functions. The originality of the work lies in finding an optimization model for minimizing the resource usage of hard real-time systems while meeting task deadlines. This assists in reducing resource over-provisioning and ensuring task schedulability within limited resources.

div.head: II. PROBLEM STATEMENT
div.p: Traditional task scheduling approaches tend to over resource provision for hard real-time systems to meet deadlines. To reduce the over-provisioning problem, we see different attempts [2], [3] by incorporating dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) and controlling the processor speed to meet the timing requirements. However, it is essential to find optimal resource allocation before applying DVS. Therefore, the problem statement of this work is the following:
"Given a hard real-time system with workload W = {T 1 , T 2 , . . . , T n }, find an optimal resource allocation Θ i to schedule all task T to minimize resource provisioning under EDF scheduling."
The problem mentioned above is described as an optimization problem. Hence, an objective function is derived to minimize resource provisioning and determine the optimal resource allocation.

div.head: III. PROPOSED RESOURCE OPTIMIZATION MODEL
div.p: According to [4], a periodic resource model, R(Π, Θ), supplies Θ amount of resource in every Π units of time. The task schedulability of a hard real-time system, C with workload W and scheduling algorithm A, can be ensured if, and only if, the maximum possible resource demand (dbf ) of C gets fulfilled by the minimum resource availability (sbf ) of R during any time interval of length t. Shin and Lee [4] have used the following equation to calculate the sbf (t) and dbf (t) function.
The dbf in a workload W = {τ i (p i , e i )} is defined by:
div.formula: dbf(W, EDF, t) = Ti∈W t p i .e i (2
div.p: Π and Θ in equation 1 indicate the resource period and supply, respectively. In the equation 2, p i and e i represent the time period and execution time of task T i .

Prior works [5] discuss energy-aware schedulability analysis to minimize resource over-provisioning; however, they lack discussion on finding an optimal resource allocation for the periodic resource model. Discovering the optimal resource amount is the preliminary step for reducing resource overprovisioning. We find that there is an opportunity to derive the resource of a periodic resource model using the linear [4] to meet the schedulability deadline of real-time tasks. We define the process of finding minimal resource allocation using lsbf(t) and ldbf(t) equations as LSDBF_RS.

However, solving these equations does not provide the optimal resource amount. Therefore, our main objective is to formulate the problem as an optimization problem and solve it to find the minimum possible resource allocation for hyperperiod (H) without affecting the schedulability of the workload.
In this work, we propose the optimal resource (OPT_RS) model to find Θ i , for all W i , that
div.formula: Minimize sbf (H) -dbf (H), subject to Ti∈W t p i .e i ≤ sbf (t), 0 < Θ ≤ Π
div.p: At hyperperiod, H (least common multiplication of all Π i of a component), the resource provisioning needs to be minimized in our optimization problem with a variable Θ i and the static values H, p i , e i and Π i . The objective function is subject to two constraints: (1) The dbf cannot exceed the sbf at any time, t to satisfy the hard deadlines, (2) The resource may vary between a range minimum Θ min > 0 and a maximum
div.formula: Θ max = Π, that is constrained by 0 < Θ i ≤ Π i .

div.head: IV. EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS
div.p: We use the SciPy optimization library to solve this resource optimization problem, which provides the value of optimum resource allocation. The set of workloads (avionics data) used in this paper is collected from [1], which contains five components listed in Table I. Figure 1 illustrates that the resource over-provisioning for OPT_RS is reduced by 15.2%, 20.2%, 21.7%, 3.6%, and 5.3% compared to LSDBF_RS in C1, C2, C3, C4, and C5 respectively. This result indicates an average of 13% reduction in resource allocation with OPT-RS. Moreover, Figure 2 highlights that OPT_RS is not only efficient in finding optimal resources but also capable of avoiding overloads. V. CONCLUSION Resource over-provisioning is a significant challenge in existing real-time embedded systems. Though this resource supply is adequate to fulfill workload requirements, it causes resource wastage.
